Subject: Search quality hypotheses and demo plan

Hi Tom / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone has a single source of truth.

Call summary (30m):
- Skyward's primary goal: improve semantic search relevance for short user queries (~3–10 tokens) across ~12k product documents; current recall@10 feels inconsistent across categories.
- Constraints: strict PII handling (no raw export outside AWS us-west-2), target latency <= 60ms p99 for single-vector queries, and pilot budget constrained to small-run proofs.
- Current infra: ElasticSearch + legacy dense vectors (768d), limited monitoring for drift.

Preliminary hypotheses / what we want to test in the pilot:
1) Increasing embedding dimensionality (768 -> 1024) improves recall@10 on short queries for product descriptions, but may increase quantization noise in compressed indexes.
2) Model choice impacts directional similarity: some models produce tighter cluster separation for SKU-level descriptions (benefit: better top-5 precision).
3) Simple prompt/context augmentation (e.g., include category token + 32-char context) boosts alignment for ambiguous short queries.

Redwood recommended baseline for evaluation (quick, low-cost POC):
- Models: Redwood-embed-small-v2 (768d) as baseline; Redwood-embed-dense-v3 (1024d) as suggested test model.
- Metrics: recall@10, MRR@10, NDCG@10, and per-category recall delta. Also capture pairwise cosine distance distribution to detect dimensionality collapse.
- Dataset: 10k sampled docs (stratified by category) + 500 labeled queries (70/30 split for eval/test).

Deliverables we propose for the pilot:
- Sample benchmark run (we'll provide example runs and scripts) — see attached sample PDF.
- Shared prompt sets (three candidate prompt variants) — attached XLSX.
- 45-minute technical deep-dive + live demo (we'll show similarity neighborhoods and tooling for drift alerts).

Next steps
1) If you're good with the scope, we can schedule the technical deep-dive next week (Vanessa/Neha/Marissa).
2) We'll run a quick benchmark on a 1k-doc subset in your environment (no data leaves your VPC) to sanity check latency and recall.
3) Procurement / contract: we'll share a short SOW and pilot pricing after the deep dive.

Attachments: semantic-bench-2026.pdf (sample run), prompt-sets-skyward.xlsx
HubSpot opp: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/0000000/DEAL-7543

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Thanks Vanessa — good notes. A couple quick questions before we lock the deep dive: 

1) Dimensionality concerns: can you quantify the expected index size change and rough p99 latency impact moving from 768d -> 1024d? We host in Elastic + a managed vector DB and need ballpark numbers for procurement.
2) Drift monitoring: what signals does Redwood surface for detecting semantic drift vs. natural category shift? We want to avoid chasing false positives when catalog mix changes weekly.
3) Data residency / PII: you mentioned pilot data can stay in our VPC — can you confirm no embeddings or raw text will be copied to Redwood's hosted environment during the pilot?

Alan (procurement) — looping you in so we can start to align on SOW/PO cadence if the technicals check out.

On Mon, May 18, 2026 at 9:14 AM Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@skyward.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Vanessa — good notes. A couple quick questions before we lock the deep dive: 
> 
> 1) Dimensionality concerns: can you quantify the expected index size change and rough p99 latency impact moving from 768d -> 1024d?

Good Q. Very rough ballparks (depends on quantization and index type):
- Raw float vectors: ~33% larger storage going 768->1024.
- With OPQ + 8-bit quantization: size delta typically ~10–18% depending on codec.
- Typical p99 query latency delta (vector lookup only) on comparable hosts: +5–12ms for 1024d vs 768d; end-to-end p99 including kNN re-ranking depends on infra but we expect to stay under your 60ms target with small-index pilots.

> 2) Drift monitoring: what signals does Redwood surface for detecting semantic drift vs. natural category shift?

We recommend a combination:
- Population-level stats: mean cosine distance per category over time; sudden shifts >2 stdev trigger alerts.
- Embedding dispersion metrics: kurtosis and average nearest-neighbor distance to detect collapse/overfitting.
- Query->top1 stability: fraction of queries whose top1 changes over rolling windows (we annotate likely UI-breaks).
- Auto-sampling: when we detect a signal, Redwood can export a small labeled sample (w/ your approval) for human review.

> 3) Data residency / PII: can you confirm no embeddings or raw text will be copied to Redwood's hosted environment during the pilot?

Confirmed for a VPC-hosted pilot: computations run in your VPC, logs are scoped to the pilot job, and we do not retain raw text or vectors beyond the pilot retention window you define. We'll provide an entry in the SOW that specifies retention = 30 days and KMS control. 

I've attached the sample benchmark PDF and prompt set XLSX. We'll also publish a shared Drive folder with the scripts we run (link above).

If that addresses everything, I'll book the 45-min tech session — proposed slots Tue 5/19 09:00 or Wed 5/20 14:00 PT. Please confirm preferred time.

—
Vanessa

Vanessa / Tom — quick note from the engineering side with proposed evaluation checklist we can run during the pilot (technical detail):

Evaluation checklist (pilot):
- Sampling: stratified 10k docs into train/holdout and ensure category proportions match production.
- Baselines: compare (A) current 768d legacy vectors (Elasticsearch), (B) Redwood-embed-small-v2 (768d), (C) Redwood-embed-dense-v3 (1024d).
- Tests: recall@10, MRR, per-category delta, paired bootstrap for significance (alpha=0.05).
- Dimensionality checks: PCA explained variance (first 20 components), average silhouette score across category clusters, and pairwise distance distribution plots to detect concentration.
- Quantization experiments: evaluate 8-bit vs 6-bit (if supported) for each model to find size/quality sweet spot.
- Drift simulation: synthetic shift by adding 10% new-category docs and measuring metric change; helps us tune thresholds for alerts.

I can attach a short eval-run script we use internally (it's a 2-page Markdown). For the demo we'll include visualizations: neighborhood inspection, per-query waterfall, and a small dashboard for weekly drift signals.

If you want, Marissa and I can run a 1k-doc quick sanity run in your VPC this week — that will give immediate numbers for size and p99.
